faq.a: Anahid is associated with the Persian form آناهید, whose core sense is goddess of water and fertility.

faq.q: What is the origin of Anahid?
faq.a: Anahid is associated with Persian. Anāhid, the New Persian form of Avestan Anāhitā, the Iranian goddess of the waters. The source record classified it as Arabic, which is incorrect.
No — the underlying form is Persian, not Arabic.
Anahid can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Persian-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Anahid should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. not established

faq.q: What does Anahid mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Anahid is rendered آناهید and carries the sense پانی اور زرخیزی کی دیوی.

faq.q: What does Anahid mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Anahid is rendered آناهید and carries the sense ایزدبانوی آب و باروری.
A romanized syllable approximation is a-na-hid. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Anahid?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Anahid, anahid. Script forms are آناهید, अनाहिद.

faq.q: Is Anahid a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
